(a) Office established. There is hereby established the city marshal's office. The purpose of this section is to do all things necessary for the city marshal's office to be recognized as a law enforcement agency or unit of the state and certified within the standards of the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Act (POST Act) as provided in O.C.G.A. § 35-8-1 et seq.
(b) Requirements. The requirements for the city marshal's office shall be as follows:
(1) All officers hired as a marshal shall be and shall maintain POST certification, or in the event a person is not POST certified on the date of hire, he or she shall have 12 months from the date of hire to become POST certified.
(2) All officers hired as a marshal must be at least 19 years of age, have a high school diploma or GED, and a valid state driver's license.
(3) All officers hired as a marshal must be of good moral character and standing in the community which shall require that no officer shall have any convictions of any misdemeanor involving moral turpitude or any convictions of any felony.
(c) Powers of arrest. An officer of the marshal's office shall have the power of arrest in the enforcement of all ordinances of the City of Peachtree Corners and laws of the State of Georgia.
(d) Duties and responsibilities.
(1) To enforce all ordinances enacted by the mayor and council of the city.
(2) To issue warnings, notices of violations, summons, and citations for violation of state laws and city ordinances.
(3) To serve warnings, notices of violation, summons, citations, subpoenas, orders, and other process issued by authority of the city and laws of the state.
(4) To investigate and collect evidence of ordinance violations.
(5) To respond to complaints of alleged ordinance violations.
(6) To appear and testify in court.
(7) To perform any follow-up work that may be necessary.
(8) To ensure proper collection of fines.
(9) To coordinate enforcement efforts concerning any department or division of the city as may be deemed necessary.
(10) To perform any other duties, including arrests for state law violations, as permitted and allowed under state law.
(11) To coordinate any outsourced public safety functions and serve as a law enforcement liaison between federal, state, county, city, or private agencies.
(12) To work in coordination with the city attorney's office on behalf of the city.
(e) Placement of position. All employees within the city marshal's office shall be at-will employees of the city, serving at the direction of the city manager, and may be removed at any time and for any reason without cause in the city manager's sole discretion.
(f) Jurisdiction. The jurisdiction of the city marshal's office shall be the entire incorporated area of the City of Peachtree Corners, Georgia.
(g) Chief marshal.
(1) There is created in the city marshal's office the position of chief marshal, which position shall be appointed by the city manager. Each additional officer in the city marshal's office shall be a deputy marshal.
(2) With prior approval of the city manager, the chief marshal shall be responsible for developing office policy and organization and shall be responsible for supervising all employees within the city marshal's office and shall also be responsible for the promulgation of all rules and regulations for the conduct, management, and control of the city marshal's office.
(Ord. No. 2023-06-258, § 1, 7-25-2023)

(a) Permits and fees.
(1) Permits for opening burning at or on development sites for the purpose of clearing land for new construction shall be obtained from the county department of fire and emergency services, office of the fire marshal. Permits shall be registered with the fire services communications center by the fire marshal's office.
(2) The applicant shall complete an application for an open burning permit issued by the fire marshal's office. The applicant shall submit a plat or site plan showing the proposed location of the pit and information relating to the proximity of any occupied or unoccupied structure.
(3) The application, if approved, shall be accompanied by a check. The check shall be made payable to the county department of fire and emergency services. The application fee shall be in an amount as established by the mayor and council from time to time.
(4) No burning shall commence prior to an inspection of the site and the pit by a representative of the county fire marshal's office. Upon approval of the pit, the permit shall be valid for a period of 30 days. Permits may be extended for increments of 15-day periods without additional fees, maximum of two extensions.
(b) Fires requiring written permits.
(1) The only type of fires permitted for the purpose of land clearing are pit fires. Non-pit fires are not permitted for land clearing in the city. All pit fires shall be conducted in strict accordance with the "Air Curtain Destructor Operating Guide and Procedures," as published by the North Georgia Region of the Environmental Protection Division, attached hereto as Exhibit A (not set out herein; Exhibit A is on file with the county).
(2) Pit fires shall comply with the following stipulations:
a. The pit shall be at least 300 feet from any occupied or habitable structure. This distance may be increased if need is assessed by the fire marshal's office and validity exists.
b. Where a site cannot be excavated to the recommended depth due to high water table and/or subsurface rock, the pit may be constructed above ground level, subject to the same state standards and procedures for a pit below ground level.
c. Only wood wastes consisting of trees, logs, large brush, stumps, leaves, and untreated lumber may be burned in the pit.
d. Leaves, sawdust or other densely packed wood wastes, paper (any type), chemically treated, coated or impregnated wood, or non-wood construction materials shall not be burned. The amount of dirt/soil mixture shall be kept to a minimum.
e. No more than one air curtain destructor is allowed to be operated within a ten-acre permitted site at one time. The air curtain destructor must be under the supervision of a trained operator at all times during operation. In the event there is a need for multiple burning pits, there shall be a minimum of 1,000 feet between each burning pit.
f. Air curtain destructors shall be able to pass an even, non-turbulent flow of air across the top of the pit. Air curtain destructors with an air duct or manifold that has been altered by bends, dents, holes, etc., and are incapable of providing an even and non-turbulent flow of air across the top of the pit shall not be approved for use.
g. The air curtain destructor shall be operated in a manner to prevent air, land or water pollution, safety/health hazards, or nuisances.
h. Tires or other rubber products, plastics, heavy oils or asphaltic base or impregnated materials shall not be used to start or maintain air curtain destructor operations.
i. No smoke emissions exceeding 40 percent opacity may be produced during operation except for a reasonable period during ignition and charging of the pit.
j. When the pit is cleared of ash, airborne particulate is to be minimized by wetting or mixing the ashes with dirt.
k. Diesel fuel or kerosene may be used to start pit fires.
(c) Types of burning allowed without a written permit. The following types of burning are allowed without a written permit:
(1) Burning of leaves and limbs and natural vegetation that may fall on one's property.
(2) Fires for the purpose of keeping warm. Warming fires shall be contained within a metal barrel of 55-gallon capacity or less. Untreated wood or lumber shall be the only material or substance permitted to be burned. The container for the warming fire shall not be less than 50 feet from any structure. No on-ground warming fires shall be permitted. (Note: The outside temperature shall be 50 degrees Fahrenheit or less.)
(3) Fires for the purpose of cooking food for human consumption.
(4) Bonfires. Permit required; no fee.
a. No person shall kindle or maintain any bonfire or authorize any such fire to be kindled or maintained on any private or public land unless the location is no less than 50 feet from a structure with a size not to exceed four cubic feet of combustible materials and 100 feet from a structure with a size not to exceed five cubic feet of combustible materials.
b. For purposes of clarification, bonfires shall be limited to activities sponsored by civic, educational, religious or other groups for purpose of celebration, etc. An example would be a high school pep rally.
c. Bonfires shall be constantly attended by a competent person until such fire is extinguished. Such person shall have a garden hose connected to a water supply, or other fire extinguishing equipment readily available for use. Access to communications to the fire department shall be maintained within 500 feet of the bonfire.
(d) Burning restrictions. The following rules govern all burning in the county, whether or not a written permit is required:
(1) The fire marshal's office may temporarily prohibit any and/or all outdoor fires when atmospheric conditions or local circumstances make such fires hazardous.
(2) No burning is permitted on Sundays or nights. Burning at construction sites for the clearing of land for new development shall not be conducted before or after daylight hours.
(3) No burning is permitted when prevailing winds are in excess of 15 miles per hour in the direction of populated areas immediately adjacent to the permitted site.
(4) No burning is permitted during an air pollution episode, such as an air pollution alert/warning/emergency declared by proper authorities.
(5) No burning is permitted when there is a fog, rain, or cloud bases that are diffused, or ill defined, or for at least one day following the passage of a cold front.
(6) No burning of solid waste or household garbage is allowed.
(7) No burning of any materials that emit a heavy dark smoke, such as rubber products, oils, roofing material, petroleum-based products, etc.
(8) No burning when smoke presents a health hazard to persons in the vicinity of the fire.
(9) No burning shall be conducted within 20 feet of flammable, combustible or explosive materials unless otherwise specified by NFPA or standard fire prevention codes.
(10) Burning of leaves, limbs, etc., that fall on a person's own property can only be conducted during daylight hours.
(11) Prior notification shall be given to the state forestry commission before any agricultural burning is conducted. The term "agricultural" refers to land zoned RA-200, as defined by the county zoning ordinance.
(12) All fires shall be constantly attended by a competent person until extinguished.
(13) There shall be a garden hose connected to a water supply or other fire extinguishing equipment readily available for use.
(e) Summary abatement. The staff of the fire marshal's office and personnel of the county department of fire and emergency services shall have the authority to summarily abate any conditions which are in violation of any of the provisions of this section, and which may constitute an immediate threat to life and property. In no event shall a pit fire or other open burning continue after the fire marshal's office has revoked the permit.

(a) Plans review. Each plan review unit will apply their respective codes and ordinances, as defined by Part A, Items No. 1, 2 and 3, of the ordinance from which this section is derived. During the review process, whenever differing code requirements or interpretations surface and cannot be resolved by the plan review staff, the following shall take place:

Each unit applies their respective regulations pursuant to the approved plans and specifications relating to the construction project. During the inspection process, whenever differing code requirements or interpretations surface and cannot be resolved by the field inspections staff, the following shall take place:
(1) The differing requirements or opinions shall be referred to the appropriate chief inspector and the field inspections supervisor of the fire marshal's office of the department of fire and emergency services for solution.
(2) If the appropriate chief inspector and the field inspections supervisor of the fire marshal's office of the department of fire and emergency services are not successful in reaching a solution, the situation shall be forwarded to the manager of the building inspections unit and the fire marshal for disposition.
(3) If the manager of the building inspections unit and the fire marshal are unable to reach a compromise, the predicament will be directed to the attention of the development division director of the department of planning and development and the assistant chief of technical services.
(4) If the development division director of the department of planning and development and the assistant chief of technical services are not able to come to agreement, it shall be referred to the chief of the department of fire and emergency services and the director of the department of planning and development.
(5) If the director of the department of planning and development and the chief of the department of fire and emergency services are unable to reach an accord, the matter shall be referred to the board of construction adjustments and appeals for final disposition.
